output.brief: The 22 Oct overrun was caused by the Q3 margin backfill, not by the platform incident or the new customer_ltv model. The backfill ran as one large update from 00:58 and held an exclusive lock on stage_orders until 04:18. The nightly merge waited 2h13m for that lock. The rest of the run took about its normal time, so it finished at 07:02. The Corvane incident (02:52–03:37) fell inside the lock wait, and no other waits were recorded. Data volume was normal. customer_ltv added only about 19 minutes, and the retention team depends on it. The backfill was approved for 13:00–17:00. The implementer's note said '1:00', and the change board chair can't tell whether that was a typo or deliberate. So I can't say why it ran overnight, and that's no basis for discipline. The change checklist never involved the nightly job's owner, and no alert watches for lock waits. Recommended: add the nightly job's owner as a required reviewer for changes to its tables, restrict writes in the 01:00–06:00 window, and alert on lock waits over 15 minutes. Keep the banner, since Finance used it correctly. Don't move to a higher tier, and don't pull customer_ltv. Don't discipline anyone until you've heard from the implementer. Confidence is high on the cause and lower on the intent.
